subject: Kestrel Health - request for executive rate exception
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@kestrelhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — follow-up & request for exception

Hi Amelia,

Appreciate the time on the call today. Kestrel's pilot numbers look strong — peak inference throughput and embedding volume exceeded what we originally forecasted, which is great to see. Based on the trajectory you shared, you fall into a high-volume tier in our Hosted API pricing model.

To move toward a contract that gets you predictable unit economics, I ran a few scenarios with Ben and the deal desk. The customer asks are: an up-front volume discount and a predictable monthly commit for 12–24 months. Your procurement team signaled a preference for a deeper rebate (they mentioned ~35%) to fit this year's budget.

Request: I'd like exec approval to offer a one-time (>20%) tiered discount off list for a 24-month committed Hosted API contract, contingent on the usage commit and minimum monthly spend in the attached MAP. The deal economics below are conservative and preserve our unit margin:
- Year 1 commit: 2.5M input tokens / month (estimated)
- Suggested concession: 28% off base token rate, or equivalent $/1M token blended rate in the term sheet
- Alternatives: 30% for a 36-month commitment; 25% for a 12-month commit + annual true-up

Attachments: kestrel_mutual_action_plan.pdf (MAM), kestrel_usage_forecast.xlsx (detailed forecast).

If this looks reasonable I can escalate to Sales Ops / Deal Desk for formal pricing and legal to draft the limited-term term sheet. Ben — any additional context for the exec request?

Thanks,
Lukas

--
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
l.meyer@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0197
From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@kestrelhealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tim Harper <tim.harper@kestrelhealth.com>, procurement@kestrelhealth.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — follow-up & request for exception

Lukas —

Thanks for the quick summary and for the materials. The pilot performed well and the team is excited. Procurement reviewed the MAP and our CFO is pushing for a deeper near-term cut given budget constraints this fiscal year.

We'd be comfortable with a 24-month commit, but to move forward this quarter we actually need a 35% discount applied to the Hosted API token rates (or an equivalent blended rate) for the first 12 months, then step down to the standard committed discount thereafter. Tim from procurement is on this thread and can share the formal PO timing.

If Redwood can meet that structure we'll sign the PO and target a July go-live for committed capacity.

—Amelia

On Sun, Jun 27, 2027 at 09:12 AM Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> (original message)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Approval required — Kestrel Health pricing concession (35% request)

Team — forwarding Kestrel's ask. TL;DR: strategic healthcare customer, strong pilot numbers, asking for 35% off list for first 12 months (then revert). They want a 24-month commit and will sign a PO this quarter if we can meet budget.

Why this matters:
- Kestrel is integrating Redwood into a revenue-critical triage workflow; expansion potential across multiple hospitals in Q3–Q4.
- Forecasted committed volume (see attachment) is high enough to justify a material concession if we can get a multi-year lock.

Options I recommend for executive consideration (ranked):
1) Approve up to 30% off list for 24 months with a minimum monthly commit and an accelerated true-up clause. Provide a capped one-time onboarding credit in lieu of 35% in year 1.
2) Approve 28% off list for 24 months (no onboarding credit).
3) If leadership wants to push to 35% for Q1 only, require a contingent higher commit and CLTV guarantee (e.g., 36-month guarantee or revenue assurance addendum).

Attached: kestrel_usage_forecast.xlsx, proposed_term_sheet_v2.pdf

Request: Stephanie / Marcus — can you weigh in with final exec guidance? If approved, I'll prepare a short memo and proposed term sheet for legal and post-approval signature routing.

-Ben

--
Ben Carter
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Approval required — Kestrel Health pricing concession (35% request)

Ben / Marcus —

Thanks for the context and attachments. I've reviewed the forecast and the proposed term structure. Given the strategic nature of the account and the probability of expansion across Kestrel's hospital groups, I'm prepared to authorize an exception within the following constraints: 

- Executive approval: up to 30% discount off standard Hosted API token rates for a 24-month committed contract (effective months 1–24).
- Required commitments: minimum monthly spend of $60k equivalent in month 1 rising to $85k by month 4, with a 12-week ramp schedule documented in the MAP.
- Legal: limited-term term sheet (attached) with an onboarding credit capped and a mandatory revenue assurance clause; no permanent list-rate change.
- Approval does NOT extend to 35% as a firm concession unless Kestrel agrees to a 36-month revenue guarantee and a signed LOI by July 9. If they accept that, re-escalate and I'll review for potential additional concession.

Lukas — please communicate these terms to Amelia and Tim. If they accept, route the updated term sheet and PO to legal and procurement, and copy me on the DocuSign.

Stephanie

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
